description: Search PubMed with full query syntax, filters, and date ranges. Returns PMIDs and optional brief summaries. Supports field-specific filters (author, journal, MeSH terms), common filters (language, species, free full text), and pagination via offset for paging through large result sets.

author.description: Filter by author name (e.g. "Smith J"). An empty string applies no filter; a value of only whitespace, invisible characters, markup, parentheses, brackets, or double quotes is rejected.

dateRange.description: Filter by date range. The filter is applied only when both `minDate` and `maxDate` are non-empty; either one empty disables the entire date range. A partial date covers its whole year or month, and a range whose `minDate` falls after its `maxDate` is rejected: `2024/06` to `2024` is valid, `2024/07` to `2024/06/30` is not.

maxDate.description: End date (YYYY/MM/DD, YYYY/MM, or YYYY). Must be a real calendar date — `2023/02/29` is rejected. Leaving it empty drops the whole date range, not just this bound; for no upper bound pass a wide sentinel such as `3000`.

minDate.description: Start date (YYYY/MM/DD, YYYY/MM, or YYYY). Must be a real calendar date — `2023/02/29` is rejected. Leaving it empty drops the whole date range, not just this bound; for no lower bound pass a wide sentinel such as `1000`.

freeFullText.description: Only include free full text articles

journal.description: Filter by journal: its NLM title abbreviation (e.g. "N Engl J Med") or ISSN; a full title matches only as NLM records it. An empty string applies no filter; a value of only whitespace, invisible characters, markup, parentheses, brackets, or double quotes is rejected.

language.description: Filter by language: its English name or three-letter NLM code (e.g. "english" or "eng"); a two-letter code such as "en" matches nothing. An empty string applies no filter; a value of only whitespace, invisible characters, markup, parentheses, brackets, or double quotes is rejected.

maxResults.description: Maximum results to return, up to 1000 per call; a larger value returns 1000 with a notice naming the next `offset`. 0 returns only `totalCount`.

meshTerms.description: Filter by MeSH headings, each searched as `"term"[MeSH Terms]`. Multiple terms are AND'd — all must match. A supplementary concept, as many drugs are, is not a heading and matches nothing here: search it in `query` as the `searchTerm` pubmed_lookup_mesh returns, such as `"dapagliflozin"[nm]`. Empty strings are skipped; an element of only whitespace, invisible characters, markup, parentheses, brackets, or double quotes is rejected.

offset.description: Result offset for pagination (0-based). PubMed serves at most the first 9999 records of a result set, so this caps at 9998; narrow the query or add filters to reach anything beyond it.

publicationTypes.description: Filter by publication type (e.g. "Review", "Clinical Trial", "Meta-Analysis"). Multiple values are OR'd — any match qualifies. Empty strings are skipped; an element of only whitespace, invisible characters, markup, parentheses, brackets, or double quotes is rejected.

query.description: PubMed search query (supports full NCBI syntax), sent as written apart from inline formatting tags such as `<i>`, which are removed. Omit it or pass an empty string to search on the filters alone, which needs `author`, `journal`, `meshTerms`, or `publicationTypes`; `all[sb]` selects the whole database for a slice by the other filters. A query given must carry a search term: a value that is blank once markup, bracketed field tags (`[pdat]`), parentheses, and invisible characters such as a zero-width space are disregarded is rejected rather than sent to PubMed.

sort.description: Sort order: relevance (default), pub_date (publication date, newest first), author (first author A–Z), or journal (journal name A–Z)

species.description: Filter by species: `humans` adds `humans[MeSH Terms]`, `animals` adds `"animals"[mh:noexp]` (animals other than humans; a record indexed for both stays in). Both match only records with MEDLINE species indexing, which preprints and ahead-of-print citations lack.

summaryCount.description: Fetch brief summaries for the top N results (0 = PMIDs only), up to 50 per call; a larger value fetches 50 with a notice. Pass the PMIDs past the cap to pubmed_fetch_articles.

name: pubmed_search_articles

appliedFilters.description: Filter values applied to the PubMed query, as sent: each text value as written, formatting tags removed, and dates in YYYY/MM/DD form

author.description: Author filter applied to the search

dateRange.description: Date range filter applied to the search

dateType.description: Applied date field used for the range filter

freeFullText.description: Whether results were restricted to free full-text articles

hasAbstract.description: Whether results were restricted to articles with abstracts

journal.description: Journal filter applied to the search

language.description: Language filter applied to the search

meshTerms.description: MeSH term filters applied to the search

publicationTypes.description: Publication type filters applied to the search

species.description: Species filter applied to the search: `humans` as `humans[MeSH Terms]`, `animals` as `"animals"[mh:noexp]`

effectiveQuery.description: The term sent to PubMed: the query as written, with a clause appended for each active filter, or the filter clauses alone, joined by AND, when no query was given. Only inline formatting tags with no attributes (`<i>`, `<b>`, `<em>`, `<strong>`, `<u>` and their closers) are removed; `&`, `<`, and `>` are sent as written.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `queue_full`: The local NCBI request queue shed the call — the queue is full, or the call cannot start before its total deadline (for example behind the cooldown that follows an NCBI 429). `ncbi_unreachable`: NCBI E-utilities failed on every attempt the retry budget allowed — retries ran out, the next backoff would overrun the total deadline, or the call made one attempt without retrying because the previous call to the same E-utility had failed on every attempt. `ncbi_rate_limited`: NCBI answered HTTP 429 (too many requests) and the call stopped on it — retries ran out, the next backoff would overrun the total deadline, or the Retry-After NCBI named outlasts the time left or the 30-second backoff cap. `ncbi_deadline_exceeded`: The total NCBI request deadline expired before NCBI answered successfully — mid-request, while queued, or during a retry backoff. `ncbi_invalid_response`: NCBI returned a body that could not be parsed (invalid XML/JSON). `ncbi_resource_not_found`: NCBI returned a structured "not found" error for the requested ID(s). `blank_query`: The query contains no search term: nothing is left once whitespace and invisible characters such as a zero-width space are disregarded. pubmed_search_articles and pubmed_europepmc_search first decode HTML entities and also disregard markup and parentheses, so `()`, ``, and ` ` hold no term there; pubmed_search_articles also disregards bracketed field tags such as `[pdat]`. On pubmed_search_articles an exactly-empty `query` is not blank: it means no query, and the search runs on its filters. `invalid_date_range`: A `dateRange` bound is not a real calendar date — a month outside 01–12, day 00, or a day past the end of its month such as `2023/02/29` — or `minDate` falls after `maxDate` once PubMed expands each partial date: `minDate` from the start of its year or month, `maxDate` to the end. `blank_filter`: An `author`, `journal`, or `language` value, or a `publicationTypes` or `meshTerms` element, holds no term once markup is removed and HTML entities are decoded — only whitespace, invisible characters such as a zero-width space, parentheses, brackets, or double quotes are left, as in `()` or `""` — so its field clause would carry no term. An exactly-empty string is not blank here; it sets no filter. `no_search_term`: No `query` is given — it is omitted or an empty string — and no subject filter (`author`, `journal`, `meshTerms`, or `publicationTypes`) carries a term. `dateRange`, `language`, `species`, `hasAbstract`, and `freeFullText` narrow a search without saying what it is for, so they cannot run one alone. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

notice.description: Optional guidance when the result set does not reflect what was asked for — a field tag PubMed ignored, a phrase it matched nothing for (with advice by the clause's field), a dateRange dropped for having one bound, no matches at all, paging past the end, a page that ends at PubMed's 9,999-record window with matches past it that no `offset` reaches, or a `maxResults` or `summaryCount` past its per-call cap, served at the cap. Absent when nothing applies.

query.description: Original query; empty when the search ran on the filters alone

summaries.description: Brief summaries (empty array when summaryCount is 0)

authors.description: Author string — the first three of the record's own authors, then "et al.". On an NCBI Bookshelf chapter these are the chapter's authors; the book's editors are in `editors`.

bookTitle.description: Title of the book an NCBI Bookshelf record belongs to, e.g. "GeneReviews(®)". Present instead of `source` on a book record; absent on a journal article.

docType.description: What PubMed classifies this record as: "chapter" or "book" for an NCBI Bookshelf record, "citation" for an ordinary journal article. Absent when PubMed supplies none.

doi.description: DOI, cased as NCBI reports it. DOIs are case-insensitive by spec and no case normalization is applied here, so casing can differ from a Europe PMC-sourced `doi` — compare the two case-insensitively. Absent when the record has none.

editors.description: Editors of the containing book, kept out of `authors` so they cannot displace the record's own authors. Absent on a journal article and on a book that credits no editors.

items.description: One editor, "Surname Initials" as ESummary renders it

epubDate.description: Electronic publication date — when the article went online, often ahead of the issue `pubDate` names — in ISO 8601 at the precision PubMed states, normally `YYYY-MM-DD`. Absent when PubMed records none.

pmcId.description: PubMed Central ID (`PMC` prefix) of the record's PMC copy. Absent when the record has none.

pmcUrl.description: Link to the record's PMC copy; present exactly when `pmcId` is.

pubDate.description: Publication date as PubMed states it, in ISO 8601 at that precision: `2026`, `2026-12`, or `2026-09-30`. A stated range is an interval `start/end` — `2026-09/2026-10` for a bimonthly issue, `1994/1995`, `2006-12-12/2007-01-01` — and a season reads as its year; every form opens with the four-digit year. On an NCBI Bookshelf chapter (`docType` "chapter") it is the chapter's own date — its last revision, otherwise its contribution — not the year its book began. Absent when PubMed states no date with a year.

publisherName.description: Publisher of the book an NCBI Bookshelf record belongs to. Present only on a book record; absent on a journal article.

pubmedUrl.description: Link to the record's PubMed page; present on every row.

source.description: Journal the article appeared in. Absent on an NCBI Bookshelf record, which has no journal — its venue is in `bookTitle` and `publisherName` instead, and `docType` says which kind of record it is.

title: Pubmed Search Articles
